title: The influence of estrogen in the menstrual cycle on biomechanic changes in running style during running-induced fatigue in female long-distance runners
summary:
Running is a very popular sport, but prolonged running can lead to fatigue and changes in running motion. These changes can affect both performance and the risk of injury. Women represent a large proportion of the running population, yet little research has been done to date on whether and how the natural menstrual cycle affects running and fatigue behaviour.
The menstrual cycle is accompanied by natural fluctuations in certain hormones. These hormones can influence the properties of muscles, tendons and ligaments, among other things, and thus possibly also how women move when running – especially when they become fatigued. The aim of this study is to investigate whether fatigue responses during running differ in specific phases of the menstrual cycle.
Twenty-four healthy female long-distance runners with regular menstrual cycles are participating in the study. Each participant completes two 10 km runs on a treadmill, each in a different phase of their menstrual cycle. During the runs, running movement, muscle activity, breathing and heart rate, among other things, are measured. In addition, blood samples are taken to determine hormone concentrations and classify the menstrual cycle phases.
The results should contribute to a better understanding of whether and how the menstrual cycle affects fatigue and running movement. In the long term, these findings could help to design training for female runners more individualised and targeted.

interventions.name: Female runners with a natural menstrual cycle complete a lower limb strength assessment and two intensive 10 km runs with 3D motion analysis and respiratory gas analysis on a treadmill in two specific menstrual cycle phases (early vs. late follicular phase). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Regular participation in running (from middle distance ≥ 800 m) or triathlon
- Knowledge of the current 10 km best time
- Natural regular menstrual cycle:
     o Cycle length between 21 and 35 days with fluctuations of less than 8 days
     o  No hormonal contraception (for at least 3 months)
- Progesterone level in the blood of > 16 nmol/L during the mid-luteal phase
Exclusion criteria:
- Injuries of the lower extremities in the last 6 months that have resulted in a running break of more than one week
- Chronic diseases or neurological disorders affecting mobility or resilience (e.g. osteoarthritis, Parkinson's disease)
- Existing pregnancy
- Breastfeeding (in the case of a previous pregnancy, less than 12 months after the end of breastfeeding)
- Known cycle disorders or gynaecological/endocrinological diseases, in particular:
     o Amenorrhoea (> 3 months)
     o Absence or severely irregular menstrual cycle
     o Endometriosis
     o Polycystic ovary syndrome
     o Thyroid disorders
